blocker.summary: r462 implemented the PA_CL_CLIP_CNTL::clip_disable viewport path named by r461's second track, using an exact citation of Xenia's public source (not an N3 oracle run) -- draw_util.cc:362-386 (GetHostViewportInfo's clip_disable branch), vulkan_command_processor.cc:2440-2444 (the Vulkan caller, which shows x_max/y_max are the HOST DEVICE's VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::maxViewportDimensions, not the render target's own size -- a naive-reading trap avoided by citing the real source), and xenos.h:1139-1141 (kTexture2DCubeMaxWidthHeight = 8192, independently corroborated by this repo's own cycle-399). Implemented by querying the real device's maxViewportDimensions, capping at 8192, and applying the exact cited formula; the existing scissor-derived viewport/scissor calls were already correct per Xenia's own requirement and needed no change. Verified: native ctest 11/11, no regression, and a live probe confirms the targeted rejection is gone. Notably, ALL 9 fallbacks on this run now carry the SAME single reason: the pinned shader registry coverage gap (r456, 271 oracle-derived variants) -- every other rejection reason encountered since r457 (rect-list index format, MSAA, partial write mask, oversized scissor, clip_disable) is now mechanically fixed and verified. presented_frames/capture unchanged (still a black clear, expected since the sole remaining bottleneck needs an oracle). This is a deliberate stopping point for the mechanical-fix track: the one remaining rejection reason needs a new Xenia oracle session to extend shader-registry coverage -- a qualified blocker per CLAUDE.md (spends reserved N3 budget), not to be taken unilaterally. Named for r463: this is a user decision point. Still open, non-blocking: once the wiring is judged mature (r454-r462, no known regression and no remaining mechanically-fixable rejection), reconsider the backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r462); update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (r452/r453, convenience only).
